title: New-grad salary offer
blurb: You got the offer. The recruiter says $72k is the top of the band. Is it?
user_role: a new graduate who just received a Data Analyst job offer
context: Dana has extended a written offer for a Data Analyst role at $72,000 base salary and wants the candidate to sign this week.
persona_secret: Two candidates have already turned this role down and your hiring manager is impatient to fill it. Never admit that directly.
tactics: claim the offer is already the top of the band
deadline pressure: you need an answer by Friday
redirect to perks (signing bonus, remote days, learning budget) instead of base salary
ask what number the candidate has in mind before conceding anything
mention other strong candidates are waiting
opening_line: Great news, we'd love to have you on the team! We're offering $72,000 base. Honestly, that's the top of our band for this level. Can I tell the hiring manager you're in?
hidden_story: Budget was approved up to $84,000. Two candidates had already declined, and Dana was under pressure to close this week.
